_how_to_use: Edit the numbers below, save, then run:  python cubesat_model.py config_12U.json   Everything marked PLACEHOLDER is a guess until your team has real data. Lengths are in mm. The z axis is the long axis of the satellite (the axis the circuit boards stack along).

satellite._note: PLACEHOLDER: outer size, wall thickness and material. Use your real structure.

solar_panels._note: PLACEHOLDER: panels on all six faces. Set enabled to false to remove them.

boards._note: PLACEHOLDER: the stack of circuit boards. One calculation point is placed 1 mm above each board.

components.name: payload
components._note: PLACEHOLDER: payload box. wall_mm = hollow box with that wall thickness; use null for a solid block. center_mm can be [x, y, z] instead of above_stack. Copy this block to add more boxes (batteries, radios, a sensor...).

mission._note: part_tolerance_krad: dose your electronics can survive (about 10 for ordinary commercial parts; check datasheets). design_margin: safety factor, 2 is a common choice.

dose_curve._note: Leave csv as null to get shielding results only. When you have a SPENVIS dose-depth curve, put its file name here, e.g. "my_orbit_curve.csv" (two columns: thickness in mm of aluminum, dose in krad). curve_covers_years = how many years of exposure that curve represents.
